articles.title: Save $40 Off Microsoft's Professional-Grade Xbox Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller
articles.summary: Do you prefer PlayStation or Xbox controllers? I'm in the latter camp. My favorite PC controllers have always been modeled after Xbox's tried and true asymmetrical layout. And when it comes to Xbox controllers, you can't get much better than the highest end model from Microsoft itself.
body: The Elite Series 2 Core is the official premium controller for Xbox. The Core model is physically identical to the previous generation $200 Xbox Elite Series 2 controller, with integrated pro gaming features like adjustable-tension thumbsticks, wrap-around rubberized grip, and shorter hair trigger locks. The only difference is that the original Elite controller comes with more accessories: extra sets of paddles, thumbsticks, D-pad, and a travel case. The Elite Series 2 Core doesn't come with any of those accessories. You can buy them separately as a component pack for $59.99.

IGN's Jacqueline Thomas reported on rumored leaks that the Elite Series 3 release might be on the horizon. I'm not very optimistic, however, that the launch price will be the same as the Xbox Series 2 controller when it first released at $179.99. Given that the price of the Elite Series 2 with component pack is $200, I expect the same price or higher.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: Disney Will Air a Real-Time, Animated Version of the 2027 Super Bowl Set in the Star Wars Universe
articles.summary: Disney and the NFL have confirmed a real-time, animated “alternate telecast” of Super Bowl LXI, set in the Star Wars galaxy, will stream live on Disney+ and the ESPN App (and air on Disney Channel and Disney XD) on February 14, 2027.
body: Dubbed “Star Wars Funday Football”, the company notes this production will give “fans of all ages a new way to experience ESPN’s first-ever Super Bowl production.”

However, while Star Wars Funday Football will be the first animated alternate broadcast of a Super Bowl, it will otherwise be the fourth of its kind from ESPN, Disney, and the NFL (following the Sports Emmy Award-winning Toy Story Funday Football in 2023, The Simpsons Funday Football in 2024, and Monsters Funday Football in 2025).

The broadcasts are made possible via “data visualization technology” from Sony’s Beyond Sports, which converts real-time player tracking data into animation in real-time. If you haven’t seen it in action, it converts the spectacle of real human skill and athleticism into what looks like a licensed mobile game, only you can’t affect the outcome, and it goes for three hours.

With 2027 marking the 50th anniversary of Star Wars, Star Wars Funday Football will air just five days before a newly restored version of the original 1977 Star Wars returns to cinemas on February 19, 2027.

articles.title: "This act is intended to demonstrate solidarity with Palestine" - Umurangi Generation studio blocks new game Penguin Colony from being sold in Israel
articles.summary: Origame Digital, the studio behind 2020's critically acclaimed Umurangi Generation, has just released a new game but banned it from being sold in Israel.
body: Penguin Colony is a Lovecraftian horror game experienced through the eyes of a penguin, based on author H.P. Lovecraft's story At the Mountains of Madness. Fellow Traveller, the game's publisher, confirmed that Penguin Colony is not on sale in Israel in a Steam community thread. The thread was created by a Steam user living in Israel wondering if the game had been delisted from Steam.

"While in general we seek to bring our games to as many potential players as possible, we believe strongly that developers have the right to control where their games are sold," Fellow Traveller replied. "In this case, the developer asked us to block sale in Israel. In the absence of more organised sanctions, this act is intended to demonstrate solidarity with Palestine. We fully support their decision."

That message is further reinforced by Penguin Colony itself, which features a post-credits scene that makes clear the studio's stance on Israel's genocide of the Palenstinan people. As shared online, the message reads: "The cowardice of the Games Industry during the ongoing genocide of Palestine by Isreal will be recorded by the art it makes."

articles.title: 5 Best Halloween 'Peanuts' Comics That Don't Involve the Great Pumpkin
articles.summary: Halloween in Charles Schulz's Peanuts frequently meant it was time for another run at the Great Pumpkin. This running gag, introduced in 1959, was sort of like Schulz's answer to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot.
body: The roots of the Great Pumpkin joke seem to lie in a comic strip from Oct. 23, 1959. Charlie Brown complains to Patty that he couldn't get a Halloween mask from the store... because they'd already moved on to selling all their Christmas decorations.

It's interesting to see this complaint in a comic strip from 67 years ago. We often assume that the aggressive commercialization of Christmas in particular has gotten worse in the 21st century, but it turns out it was still an issue when our grandparents were young.

It also helps bring the Great Pumpkin into context as a parody of that commercialization. As time went on and Schulz evolved the joke, the Great Pumpkin picked up enough of its own unique lore that it moved away from its origins. In its first appearance, it's more obviously a case of a little kid getting Halloween and Christmas confused courtesy of consumerism. By the '70s, it had become more of a commentary on religious culture and blind faith, with Linus occasionally going so far as to proselytize door-to-door on the Great Pumpkin’s behalf.

articles.title: Clayface Stars Praise Batman: The Animated Series and Ron Perlman's 'Amazing' Performance as the DC Villain
articles.summary: Clayface stars Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie were big fans of Batman: The Animated Series growing up in the UK, recalling how they would rush home to watch it after school. “It was a ritual for a long time,” Ackie told IGN.
body: Horror filmmaker Mike Flanagan’s original screenplay for Clayface drew its inspiration directly from the Batman: The Animated Series episode “Feat of Clay” that reimagined how actor Matt Hagen became Clayface.
“It was really interesting being involved with this where I got to revisit that ‘ Feat of Clay ’ episode,” Rhys Harries said, heaping praise on Clayface voice actor Ron Perlman.

Ackie, who was paired with Rhys Harries for our interview, added, “But you feel so sorry for him. I think what is amazing is that we hold onto the idea of the tragedy of this character in this iteration of Clayface. And it feels, like you said, quite heartfelt at the same time as being absolutely horrific.”
For more on Clayface and the future of the DCU, be sure to read my interview with DC Studios co-chairman and co-CEO Peter Safran.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Is Soaring, But Midnight Is Struggling
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Midnight expansion feels like it's in a state of crisis by comparison. The two different versions of WoW couldn't be in more different places.
body: Midnight seems to be in the opposite corner. Its latest content update, patch 12.1.5, went live October 13. In addition to new story quests that continue the expansion's main narrative, it added a new single-boss raid and a long-teased mega delve (officially called a labyrinth) that gives solo-focused players an almost raid-like experience.

Unfortunately, the patch was released in a bug-riddled state. The Kindo'jan labyrinth, arguably the patch's biggest feature, saw players running into issue after issue. Some players complained about not earning credit for boss kills and being unable to collect rewards. One particularly nasty bug had players falling through the floor of the labyrinth's final boss arena, making it so the labyrinth couldn't be completed. Other players cited issues with delve companion Valeera dying too quickly or failing to do proper boss mechanics.

articles.title: You Don’t Need An Expensive Console Or High-End PC To Play Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expensive than ever, you might be wondering if there is another way to play. Thankfully, there is, but there are a few things you need to know before jumping in.
body: Nvidia's streaming service, GeForce Now, will be another way to play Modern Warfare 4 without any expensive hardware like a new console or high-end PC. Or at least we think so. Nvidia hasn't outright confirmed this, but people are playing the campaign early access via GeForce Now, so it stands to reason that it will be officially supported at launch for everyone.
After buying the game outright, you'll be able to stream MW4 on GeForce Now by subscribing to one of the platform's membership tiers.

GeForce Now has multiple tiers, including a free ad-supported membership. There are also $10/month and $20/month tiers with no ads and higher-fidelity experiences. There are also day passes available.

Before subscribing to Game Pass or GeForce Now, people should know that playing a twitch shooter like Modern Warfare 4 over the internet might not always be the perfect experience. After all, a cloud service works best with a strong and stable connection, and that's not always a guarantee. However, many people report good experiences, and as always, your mileage may vary.

articles.title: 3 Video Games Where Your Choices Actually Make a Difference
articles.summary: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when…
body: Large-scale narrative branches are engaging for a reason. They're satisfying, and they make you feel a sense of influence over events and characters you care about. Like with video game romance, however, they have become somewhat stale and predictable in form. So for this list, I decided to look at three games that use branching narratives in bolder and unexpected ways.

Zero Parades: For Dead Spies is the rare piece of interactive media where your choices matter not just for how they influence the story, but for how they shape your actions, too. Hershel, the protagonist of the piece, is a spy. Or, was a spy. A series of catastrophic incidents happened, and she finds herself decommissioned, in a room with a comatose person, and without any idea how she got here. There's a very dangerous game afoot in the fictional town of Portofiro, Zero Parades ' setting, and your job is figuring it out and possibly even finding redemption. Maybe. If you can manage it.
points: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game?
Large-scale narrative branches are engaging for a reason.

articles.title: This LA Noire Spinoff Idea Sounds Incredible
articles.summary: British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty great. Speaking to BAFTA Games, Kohli said he would like to see the franchise return with a spinoff that takes players through different time periods, as a cop, as they investigate different…
body: One such setting could be Victorian England, with a storyline focused on hunting down Jack the Ripper, Kohli said. Another could take players to the '80s in California as they pursue the Night Stalker, the actor added.
"We could jump around and be a cop in different times. I would be down for that," Kohli said. "I loved it. I adored L.A. Noire."

In particular, Kohli said he was a big fan of developer Team Bondi's facial-capture system which created lifelike expressions in the game, down to granular details like how a person’s eyebrows might move.

In a game where players had to read people's facial expressions, this was a big deal, and one can only imagine how much further the technology could go today. However, Kohli said he wants a new L.A. Noire game with the same tech and the same engine.

articles.title: 'Red Dead Redemption' 2 Mod Is 'Shadow of Mordor' Meets the Wild West
articles.summary: The Lord of the Rings games Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War introduced the Nemesis system, a mechanic that makes enemy orcs remember encounters with the player, develop rivalries and return seeking revenge.
body: Despite its popularity, the Nemesis system concept hasn't appeared outside the Middle-earth games, in part because Warner Bros. patented the technology in 2021, limiting how other developers could use similar mechanics.
But now, a new Red Dead Redemption 2 mod brings a similar concept to Rockstar's open-world Western, giving NPCs their own personalities, histories and reasons to hate Arthur Morgan.

Called enRAGE, the mod is available for PC and is designed to make the game's world feel more dynamic, with characters who remember the player's actions and rival outlaw factions that operate independently.

Developed by modder nicklovin99, enRAGE gives NPCs names, personality traits, family ties and backstories that stretch back years before they encounter the player. Their temperaments influence how they react to Arthur, while their memories shape whether they forgive a slight or seek revenge.

articles.title: Saros Gets Boss Rush And Tons Of Difficulty Options With Zenith Update
articles.summary: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news.
body: First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area.

The new settings and difficulty modifiers, meanwhile, allow you to both reduce and increase the game's challenge, customizing it to fit your preferences. The "Slow Game Speed" setting lets you slow down the entire game so you have more time to react to projectiles, and you can tweak exactly how much it slows down and even if you want it to turn on automatically when combat starts. An "Auto-fire" setting also eliminates the need to actually pull the trigger when you aim, which can be handy when you're primarily focused on dodging incoming attacks. You can think of it almost like a Vampire Survivors-style tool.
points: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026.

articles.title: Moonlighter dev delays Steam playtest for its "Tower Defensevania" ReVamp over concerns that AI copycats might clone it before launch
articles.summary: Digital Sun - the indie studio behind moreish roguelike Moonlighter and moody RTS Cataclismo - has delayed a planned Steam playtest for its next game, ReVamp, citing concerns over "games being reverse-engineered, cloned and published before the original is even out."
body: The developer was planning to let folks into its vampiric "Tower Defensevania" ReVamp near the end of this spooky month, but a new trend of gen-AI copycats cloning both old and unreleased games left the studio worried.

"So many of you signed up for ReVamp's first playtest here on Steam (thank you!), but we've decided to start with something more contained on our Discord, with the public playtest coming a bit later," the developer wrote in a recent Steam blog post.

From here, Digital Sun will grant access to ReVamp's first playtest in waves starting from the 29th of October, via Discord. "Even if you don't get in right away, we'd love for you to join the conversation around ReVamp as we let more players in. We hope to open the public playtest around January. To everyone who requested access here on Steam: we're sorry for the change of plans, and thank you for your patience," the studio added.
ReVamp launches in full on 25th March, 2027. Here's hoping the move can successfully shoo away any would-be clones.

articles.title: Moonlighter studio won't host a public playtest of its next game due to rampant AI-led cloning: 'We know we're not the only developers feeling this way'
articles.summary: The studio behind the Moonlighter series has announced it will no longer host a public playtest for its forthcoming roguelike due to fears it will be "reverse-engineered, cloned and published".
body: "With launch still months away, sharing a build with tens of thousands of players feels like too big a risk," Digital Sun Games' marketing manager Israel Mallén told PC Gamer. The game under discussion is ReVamp, a "tower defensevania" roguelike due for release in March 2027.
"We know we're not the only developers feeling this way, and the more this is talked about, the more likely platforms are to step in."

In its public announcement Digital Sun Games was fairly blunt. "We've been concerned by recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned and published before the original is even out. With launch still months away, a large public build of ReVamp felt like too big a risk."

Last week the studio behind Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled plans to roll out a public demo for Steam Next Fest due to similar fears. "We're concerned the demo's content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game's presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools, and that such works could be released before launch," a spokesperson for the studio wrote.

videos.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Review
videos.summary: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.
body: "Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen’s avalanche of new content is an icy salve for the burns left by a modern world full of incremental live-service updates. Trudging through the oppressive snowdrifts of this charming new region for dozens of hours felt like uncovering a past where games dropped meaty, activity-filled expansions all the time – fitting for a game so spiritually linked to a version of itself from 14 years ago. It's not all divine, as the campaign spends far too much of its final moments driving on repetitive tasks and its new Spoils slot machine makes the endgame gear hunt more lifeless than the frozen wastes you scrounge them from. But the journey, full of new and interesting characters, vibrant and violent enemies, and the wonderful wreckage of a bygone civilization, is an engrossing adventure worth the investment."

videos.title: Saros - Zenith Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: SAROS™: Zenith is out now, available to all SAROS owners at no additional cost.
body: Take on Overlord Rush, a new mode where you race to defeat the powerful Overlords from SAROS one after another. Choose from three Sets: Incursion Set and Ascension Set each pit you against three Overlords, while Totality Set lines up all eight in one continuous gauntlet. Post your best score and compete with friends and players around the world on integrated leaderboards.*

After clearing SAROS, enter the Eclipse Layers, a New Game+ mode that sends you back into Carcosa for a more intense version of the game with altered rules, including a minimum threshold of Trial Modifiers. The more Trials you take on, the bigger Arjun’s Crown becomes, and the higher your Crown level, the more you’ll uncover from 12 hidden Visions left behind by an ancient king.
